_README: Preset for the onset-asynchrony task run as RISING FIGURE vs NOTHING THAT RECURS.
Same Config as asynchrony_config.json; only the 'asynchrony' section differs:
orders        ['rising']    one present condition: the element ascends in frequency,
component i starting i*step after the lowest. No order
contrast, so the whole session pays for one ladder and every
cell gets 20 present + 20 absent instead of 10.
absent_class  'roving'      a 'no' trial carries one time-aligned group per element, on a
fresh set of channels drawn from the WHOLE pool each time. That
is what makes the two classes envelope-matched: a group starts
just as often in both, and only whether it RECURS differs.
absent_order  'redrawn'     and that group's within-element order is drawn fresh at every
element too. A permutation does not change the multiset of
onset times inside an element, so the envelope stays matched to
the last sample -- but without it every group in a 'no' trial is
the same rising chirp on new pitches, and a run of identical
shapes is itself something to hear. With it, a 'no' trial has no
pitch that returns, no set that returns and no shape that
returns. Section [0b] of the audit measures all three.
The alternative absent class is 'incoherent' (no aligned group anywhere -- the purest cloud).
It is one flag away:  --async-set absent_class=incoherent  . It is not the default because
its machine ceiling is a U: a learnt observer reads it at d' = +1.34 at 0 ms and +0.62 at
4 ms (the present element is a chord and a chord is a level event), and again at +0.52 at
16 ms (an evenly spaced group is a regular pulse train and a random scatter is not). Only
8 and 12 ms are clean. See verification/asynchrony_rising_seed_sweep.txt.
pilot_config.json and asynchrony_config.json are untouched by this file.
